name: Everest Group
description: Everest underwrites reinsurance, meaning it sells insurance to other insurers, and also writes primary commercial insurance, mostly through wholesale and specialty channels. It collects premiums up front, pays claims later, and earns investment income on the money in between. Gross written premiums were $17.7 billion in 2025, 72% reinsurance and 27% insurance. Profit comes from two places: underwriting (premiums less claims and expenses) and investment income of $2.1 billion. In October 2025 it agreed to sell renewal rights on much of its US, UK, EU and Asia-Pacific commercial retail insurance to AIG to refocus on reinsurance and wholesale/specialty.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC 6331 (Fire, Marine & Casualty Insurance). The box says reinsurer, but 27% of premiums are direct insurance, and that half is where the losses were in 2024 and 2025.

businessLines.name: Reinsurance
businessLines.how: Insurers (cedents) pay a premium, either a fixed share of their book (pro rata) or for cover above a loss threshold (excess of loss), and Everest pays a ceding commission (25.2% of premium in 2025) plus claims; profit is what is left, plus interest earned on the float until claims are paid. Results swing with catastrophes and casualty reserve development.
businessLines.description: Treaty and facultative property, casualty and financial-lines reinsurance sold to insurers, through brokers and directly. Renamed Reinsurance Treaty from 2026.

businessLines.name: Insurance
businessLines.how: Businesses buy policies (through brokers and agents) and pay premiums; Everest pays commissions (13.1% of premium) and claims. Casualty lines have long-tail claims, so loss estimates are revised for years.
businessLines.description: Primary commercial insurance (specialty, wholesale, and retail lines now being sold to AIG). From 2026 reported as Global Wholesale & Specialty plus Legacy.

businessLines.name: Investments (not a segment)
businessLines.how: Interest and dividends on the invested premiums and shareholders' capital; grows with the size of the float and with yields.
businessLines.description: Net investment income $2,124M FY2025 vs $1,954M FY2024; $1,091M H1 2026.

brands.share: Reinsurance 72.4% of FY2025 gross written premiums

brands.share: Insurance 27.1% of FY2025 gross written premiums
